scope: Sectional review of package entrypoints, configuration, isolated service ownership and predecessor upgrade safety. Full deployment, release distribution, platform support and installed-client acceptance remain unverified.

obligations.heading: Nix
obligations.acceptance: Build the package in a fresh checkout, run its binary outside the source tree, and export config schema with no daemon or archive. Generated module options agree with that binary; only supported commands are advertised. This does not qualify the later static release binary or installed service.

obligations.heading: Nix
obligations.acceptance: Run packaged entrypoints and catalog export without a running daemon or database. Compare generated module options with the same candidate Config and defaults; an unsupported service/source request fails module validation instead of enabling a stub.

obligations.heading: Concurrency
obligations.acceptance: Use two isolated archives: the package wrapper selects its configured archive for CLI and MCP, an explicit --archive overrides it, and status/errors name the selected directory. Each request reaches only that archive daemon. Demo creation refuses an existing unowned directory and leaves real archives untouched.

obligations.heading: 10. Configuration
obligations.acceptance: Reject unknown TOML keys before component startup, compare Rust and generated Nix defaults, and observe status using that same parsed configuration. Conflicting environment connection values cannot override the supplied TOML; secrets remain file references and are not emitted in generated config or diagnostics.

obligations.heading: Minimum executable bootstrap
obligations.acceptance: Start two candidate stacks with separate state and socket endpoints; each client reaches its own daemon. Occupied endpoints fail without adoption. Stop and failed-start cleanup affect only the recorded owned processes/state; an unrelated listener and sentinel archive survive.

obligations.heading: Nix
obligations.acceptance: Start two isolated Postgres/NATS/API stacks using rendered TOML, prove database-role separation, restart each, and stop one without affecting the other or external services. Inject partial startup failure and an occupied endpoint; unwind only resources started by that invocation.

obligations.heading: Source-tree disposition
obligations.acceptance: Inspect direct and transitive consumers and local overrides against the replacement candidate. Both locked builds and a deliberate input update retain an immutable predecessor choice until explicit cutover; Python imports, contract generators and service modules are tested through their actual callers. An isolated package build alone cannot settle this acceptance.
